text_en: Jinshi Data, October 9 — According to a Financial Times report, Germany plans to nominate a candidate to succeed outgoing European Central Bank Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel, a decision that means Germany will effectively withdraw from the race for the next ECB president. People familiar with the matter said Germany's finance minister told other euro-area finance ministers in Luxembourg on Thursday evening that Berlin would soon propose a replacement for Schnabel. Schnabel will leave early in January 2027 to head the Monetary and Capital Markets Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF). In addition, current President Christine Lagarde is expected to possibly leave early before her formal term ends in October 2027, while Chief Economist Philip Lane's term will end in late May 2027.
